title: Policy 2021-02 central fill: who may act, licensure, DEA rules, where the filled prescription goes, and what may not be centrally filled
rule_summary: Section IV of Board Policy 2021-02 (adopted 2/19/21; revised 4/7/22 and 2/6/25) states that retail pharmacies licensed by the Board may serve as central fill pharmacies for other Board-licensed retail pharmacies, and a central fill pharmacy may provide central filling for one or more pharmacies. When one retail pharmacy receives a prescription and a second pharmacy prepares and subsequently delivers the filled prescription to the first retail pharmacy for dispensing to the patient, the second pharmacy is engaging in central fill activity; the policy refers readers to the full DEA definition and requirements for a central fill pharmacy. Its requirements are: (i) any central fill pharmacy dispensing medications into, within, or from Massachusetts to participating pharmacies must be licensed by Massachusetts as a resident or non-resident retail pharmacy; (ii) participating pharmacies that dispense federally controlled substances (Schedules II-V) must follow DEA regulations for central fill pharmacies and be registered with DEA, and, except as noted, must handle the central filling of Massachusetts Schedule VI controlled substances in the same manner as the DEA regulations outline for Schedule II-V, although the phrase "central fill" is not required to be added to Schedule VI prescriptions; (iii) centrally filled Schedule II-V controlled substances must be delivered to the pharmacy where the prescription originated for final dispensing to the patient; (iv) centrally filled Schedule VI controlled substances, with the exception of drugs (i.e., gabapentin) requiring reporting to the Prescription Monitoring Program, may be delivered or shipped directly to the patient from the central fill pharmacy; (v) the central filling of compounded sterile preparations or complex non-sterile preparations to be dispensed into, within, or from Massachusetts is prohibited; and (vi) participants must maintain a policy and procedure regarding the handling of medications that have not been dispensed to patients.
exam_relevance: Tests who may act as a central fill pharmacy under Board policy, its Massachusetts licence, the DEA rules and registration for Schedules II-V, where each centrally filled prescription may go, how Schedule VI and monitoring-program drugs are handled, and the ban on centrally filling sterile and complex non-sterile compounded preparations.

authority.name: Board of Registration in Pharmacy Policy 2021-02: Shared Pharmacy Service Models Including Central Fill, Remote Processing, and Telepharmacy (adopted 2/19/21; revised 4/7/22 and 2/6/25)

exceptions: Centrally filled Schedule VI drugs may be delivered or shipped directly to the patient from the central fill pharmacy, except drugs (i.e., gabapentin) requiring reporting to the Prescription Monitoring Program.
The phrase "central fill" is not required to be added to Schedule VI prescriptions, although Schedule VI central filling is otherwise handled as the DEA regulations outline for Schedule II-V.
common_confusions: The originating pharmacy's own licence does not cover the central fill pharmacy, which must itself hold a Massachusetts resident or non-resident retail pharmacy licence.
A lawful shared-services agreement does not permit a centrally filled Schedule II-V prescription to be shipped directly to the patient.
Schedule VI status is not blanket permission for direct shipment, because monitoring-program reportable drugs are carved out.
A Schedule VI drug is not federally controlled, yet the policy applies the DEA central fill handling to it.
